sub_graphs.title: Builder API: Block Bidding Lifecycle
sub_graphs.description: Models the end-to-end flow of proposer-builder separation: builder registration, bid submission, blinded block signing, and payload reveal.

nodes.label: Proposer Unregistered
nodes.description: Proposer has not yet registered preferences with the relay/builder network.

nodes.label: Register Proposer
nodes.description: Proposer submits signed registration containing fee_recipient, gas_limit preferences, and timestamp to relay.

nodes.label: Proposer Registered
nodes.description: Proposer registered with relay; builders can construct blocks targeting this proposer's preferences.

nodes.label: Slot Auction Open
nodes.description: Proposer's slot approaching; builders compete to submit highest-value blocks.

nodes.label: Builder Submits Bid
nodes.description: Builder submits a BuilderBid containing a blinded execution payload header and a value (ETH amount transferred to proposer).

nodes.label: Proposer Requests Header
nodes.description: Proposer calls getHeader endpoint; relay returns highest-value valid BuilderBid.

nodes.label: Blinded Header Received
nodes.description: Proposer has received blinded execution payload header; cannot see transaction contents.

nodes.label: Sign Blinded Block
nodes.description: Proposer signs beacon block containing blinded execution payload header; this commits proposer to the builder's block.

nodes.label: Submit Blinded Block to Relay
nodes.description: Proposer sends signed blinded block to relay via submitBlindedBlock endpoint.

nodes.label: Relay Reveals Full Payload
nodes.description: Relay returns full unblinded execution payload matching the signed header; proposer can now broadcast complete block.

nodes.label: Full Block Available
nodes.description: Proposer has complete beacon block with full execution payload; broadcasts to network.

edges.label: Send signed blinded block to relay

external_entities.name: Block Builder
external_entities.description: External entity constructing execution payloads and competing in the block auction via the relay.

external_entities.name: MEV Relay
external_entities.description: Trusted intermediary that holds builder bids, validates payloads, and mediates between proposers and builders.

external_entities.name: Block Proposer
external_entities.description: Validator selected to propose a block who outsources execution payload construction to builders.

sub_graphs.title: Builder API: Trust Model and Security Boundaries
sub_graphs.description: Models the trust relationships, commitment mechanisms, and attack vectors in the proposer-builder separation design.

nodes.label: Proposer Trusts Relay
nodes.description: Proposer relies on relay to: validate builder payloads, return the highest honest bid, and reveal the correct payload after signing.

nodes.label: Proposer Signs Blinded Commitment
nodes.description: By signing the blinded block, proposer commits to the builder's execution payload header. Equivocation (signing a different block) risks slashing.

nodes.label: Proposer Committed to Builder Block
nodes.description: Proposer cannot change the execution payload without equivocating (double-signing), which would result in slashing.

nodes.label: Builder Payload Hidden
nodes.description: Transaction contents hidden from proposer via blinding; prevents proposer from front-running or censoring specific transactions.

nodes.label: Relay Validates Builder Payload
nodes.description: Relay executes builder's payload to verify it produces the claimed value and is valid before presenting to proposer.

nodes.label: Relay Compromised
nodes.description: If relay is malicious: could return invalid bids, withhold payloads after signing, or collude with builders.

nodes.label: Builder Submits Malicious Payload
nodes.description: Builder submits payload with invalid transactions or censored content; relay validation should catch this.

edges.label: Relay withholds payload after proposer signs; proposer stuck

external_entities.name: MEV Searcher
external_entities.description: Entity identifying MEV opportunities and submitting bundles to builders for inclusion in blocks.

sub_graphs.title: Builder API: Value Transfer and Fee Economics
sub_graphs.description: Models the economic flow from MEV extraction through builder bidding to proposer payment.

nodes.label: MEV Opportunity Identified
nodes.description: Builder or searcher identifies extractable value in pending transactions (arbitrage, liquidation, sandwich, etc.).

nodes.label: Construct Optimal Block
nodes.description: Builder orders transactions to maximize extracted value; includes payment transaction to proposer's fee_recipient.

nodes.label: Compute Bid Value
nodes.description: Builder sets bid value: amount of ETH transferred to proposer. Must be competitive against other builders.

nodes.label: Bid Submitted to Relay
nodes.description: Builder's bid (value + blinded header) submitted; competes with other builders' bids.

nodes.label: Relay Selects Highest Bid
nodes.description: Relay compares all valid builder bids and returns the highest-value one to the proposer.

nodes.label: Proposer Receives Payment
nodes.description: After block inclusion, proposer's fee_recipient receives the bid value via a transaction in the execution payload.

external_entities.name: User Transactions in Mempool
external_entities.description: Pending user transactions that create MEV opportunities for builders and searchers.

ambiguities.text: The builder-specs repository README describes the high-level architecture but the specific API endpoint definitions, request/response schemas, and error codes are in the OpenAPI spec file which was not fully accessible.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume standard REST API patterns with JSON request/response bodies; specific endpoints include registerValidator, getHeader, submitBlindedBlock based on MEV-Boost architecture.

ambiguities.text: The spec states 'higher trust assumptions than PBS' but does not enumerate exactly which trust assumptions are added beyond in-protocol PBS.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the additional trust assumptions are: (1) relay honestly selects highest bid, (2) relay honestly validates payloads, (3) relay reveals payload after proposer signs, (4) relay does not collude with builders.

ambiguities.text: No specification of what happens if the relay fails to return a payload after the proposer has signed the blinded block.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume proposer loses the slot (cannot propose a different block without equivocation/slashing); this is a known liveness risk of the builder API design.

implicit_assumptions.description: The relay is trusted to honestly validate builder payloads, select the highest-value bid, and reveal the full payload after proposer commitment.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Relay could steal MEV by front-running, return invalid payloads causing proposer to miss slots, or collude with specific builders to exclude competitors.

implicit_assumptions.description: Builders cannot observe the blinded header contents after proposer signing but before payload reveal to manipulate the final payload.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Builder could substitute a different payload after seeing the proposer's commitment, potentially including harmful transactions.

implicit_assumptions.description: Relays are available and responsive within the slot timing constraints (~12 seconds per slot).
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Proposers fall back to local block building, losing MEV revenue but maintaining liveness. If fallback is not implemented, proposers miss slots.
